posts.title: Between Austerity and Redistribution: Tax Politics in Seattle
posts.description: As community-labor coalitions press local governments to tax the rich, who pays and who benefits become linked battles. Drawing on the case of Seattle's JumpStart tax on large corporations, Selen Güler shows that building fairness into who pays can take years, while the fairness promised in spending proves far easier to undo. posts.title: What It Takes to Keep Trees Alive in Urban Bangladesh
posts.description: Tree-planting campaigns promise greener cities, but their success depends on more than planting targets. Drawing on their municipal experience in Dhaka, Efadul Huq and Mohammad Azaz show how inter-agency non-cooperation produces land scarcity, municipal rules obstruct community stewardship, and how planting programs prioritize visibility over long-term survival. posts.title: A De Facto Subsidized Market-Led Activity: The Political-Economy Rationale of Affordable Housing Provision in Beirut
posts.description: A contradictory form of affordable housing has taken root in Beirut, based on informally repurposed deteriorated structures for short-term use and “rent intermediaries” who often displace owners. This recurring configuration intermingles profit realization with subsidized access, giving rise to a compelling case study of the diverse factors influencing housing affordability.
